findings.reason: without a stage predicate on the retirement rule, the section's own negative control and its migration branch cannot both pass, and the worker must guess which clause governs.
findings.text: s11's first clause requires that the step returning a source "retires that name in the same step, so that step leaves no live name without a source", while its reconciliation clause requires the same population to be "retired … if it is exhausted, or ha[ve] its source bound back if it is not", and its planted control requires "a planted accepted name's source left bound". A worker cannot satisfy all three: retiring on every return retires the accepted name, whose source the control says must stay bound (the live graph today holds three sourceless `accepted` names), and rebinding the non-exhausted ones contradicts the universal rule; the global "leaves no live name without a source" is also unreachable for the ten names that already lacked a source before the incident and that this step never touches

findings.reason: the only quantitative measure closing s11 passes on non-repair, so the section could be retired with every stranded name still live.
findings.text: s11's population target reads "the count of live names without a source, by the repository's own enumeration, is back to 10 or each further one is listed", which no outcome can fail, and the enumeration it names takes a signed `exhausted_exempt_ids` exemption (`imas_codex/standard_names/source_invariant.py:204`), so the target can also be met by excusing the seventeen exhausted names instead of retiring them
